assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting and then observing a new class of quantum matter, in which the bulk is gapped but the edges or surfaces carry protected conducting states, is original, conceptually clean and has reshaped condensed-matter physics, from Z2 classification to materials discovery. It is a theory-experiment story of the kind the physics prize has rewarded.
assessment.attribution: A fair configuration separates the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its Z2 classification (Kane and Mele) from the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells (Molenkamp, with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal being a key theory ingredient). Hasan is credited for three-dimensional surface-state work and could compete for the experimental slot; BHZ is not in the supplied credit list, so allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of independent confirmation across HgTe, Bi-based and other materials, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is not in the supplied names.
Whether the 3D topological insulator experiments (Hasan and others) should share recognition with the 2D quantum spin Hall work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory made strongly correlated electron systems, including the Mott transition, tractable through an exact infinite-dimensional limit with a self-consistent impurity problem. As someone working with statistical and stochastic models, I value a controlled mean-field limit that became a widely used computational workhorse (DMFT combined with electronic-structure methods).
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the infinite-dimensional limit (Metzner and Vollhardt), the mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem (Georges and Kotliar) and later extensions. The supplied names omit Metzner, and the credit is intrinsically spread over more than three people, so a clean trio is contestable.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use, validated against numerical methods and experiments on transition-metal oxides, though DMFT is an approximation in finite dimensions and some predictions rest on model choices.
uncertainties: Omission of Walter Metzner from the supplied credit affects fairness.
Quantitative predictive power for real materials depends on approximations in the impurity solver and on the DFT+DMFT construction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, giving direct experimental access to quantum phase transitions, many-body dynamics and quantum simulation. The Mott insulator transition and single-site-resolved microscopy are original, clear and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) supplied the proposal for the Bose-Hubbard realization; Greiner and Bloch carried out the superfluid-Mott insulator experiment and developed quantum gas microscopes; Esslinger's fermionic Hubbard work is a competing experimental claim. I have chosen a theory-experiment split but the credit is crowded and overlaps with other candidates involving Zoller and Cirac.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with extensive independent replication by many groups, with the field moving toward analog simulation of problems classical computation cannot solve; recognition is plausible now.
uncertainties: Boundary with Bose-Einstein condensation (2001) and with the trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates is blurred.
Whether Esslinger and Cirac should be included is unresolved; Jaksch is not in the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape picture, with minimal frustration and a funnel-shaped landscape, explains how a disordered chain finds its native fold, drawing on spin-glass concepts and statistical mechanics. It is a conceptual contribution to the physics of complex systems with lasting influence on protein and biomolecular physics, and a natural bridge to physics-based machine learning.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central figures for the spin-glass-inspired principle of minimal frustration and the funnel concept; Dill contributed hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model ideas that are also influential. Bryngelson and Wolynes's early spin-glass work is a further source of credit that is only partly captured by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Well established conceptually and consistent with folding kinetics and simulations, but it is partly a framework rather than a single sharply testable discovery. Fit with the physics prize rather than chemistry is arguable, and the 2024 chemistry prize for protein structure prediction may affect perceived timing.
uncertainties: Whether this is physics rather than chemistry or biology.
Allocation between Wolynes and Onuchic versus Dill, and the role of Bryngelson, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact relations for work and entropy production far from equilibrium, such as the Jarzynski equality and the Crooks relation, extend thermodynamics to small, fluctuating systems and have been verified in single-molecule and mesoscopic experiments. This is statistical physics of the kind I know well and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Credit is genuinely disputed in the literature: Evans-Cohen-Morriss and Gallavotti-Cohen on fluctuation theorems, Jarzynski's equality, Crooks's detailed fluctuation theorem and earlier work (for example Bochkov-Kuzovlev) all contribute. A compact trio is difficult to defend, and Evans appears here without Cohen, Morriss or Gallavotti.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with independent experimental confirmation in RNA unfolding, colloids and electronic circuits. However, the work is closer to a theoretical framework than to a discovery with a single decisive confirmation.
uncertainties: Priority and attribution among Evans, Cohen, Morriss, Gallavotti, Jarzynski, Crooks and earlier authors is unresolved.
The breadth of impact on mainstream physics beyond small-system thermodynamics is less clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a rapidly expanding field with a clear prediction followed by striking observations.
assessment.attribution: The core is the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model and the 2018 observations by Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (Cao et al.). Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands and Dean, Kim and others on related moire systems complicate the credit; a theory-experiment trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups since 2018 with a rich phase diagram, but the mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated, and the field is young, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity and correlated states is not settled.
Credit for Andrei and for earlier moire work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry geometric phase are foundational concepts about phase and gauge structure in quantum mechanics, now pervading condensed-matter physics (including the topological phases above), optics and chaos. They carry real conceptual weight and connect to my own background in semiclassics and quantum chaos.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) are credited for the effect, but Bohm is deceased and Ehrenberg and Siday anticipated it; Berry's 1984 phase had precursors (Pancharatnam, Longuet-Higgins, Mead-Truhlar) and was soon extended by Simon, Wilczek-Zee and Aharonov-Anandan. Combining two separate discoveries into one prize is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, with decades of experimental confirmation, such as the 1986 Tonomura work and numerous optical and molecular tests. Timeliness is no concern, though the Nobel Committee has not traditionally rewarded such foundational concepts without a clear experimental anchor.
uncertainties: Whether the two ideas form one coherent prize or two separate ones.
Priority questions around Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The conformal bootstrap in two dimensions provides exact solutions of critical phenomena and underpins modern understanding of universality and string theory worldsheets. As a statistical-physics theorist I recognize its depth and its lasting influence on field theory and critical behaviour.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov paper is the clear foundation, though Friedan, Qiu and Shenker, Cardy, Dotsenko and Fateev and others made important contributions. The trio is natural but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed through exact solutions and numerical checks on models such as the Ising and Potts systems, with decades of use. The Nobel Committee has historically favored experimentally anchored discoveries, so this pure theory is a harder fit.
uncertainties: Fit of a mainly mathematical theory with the prize criteria.
Credit for Cardy, Friedan, Qiu, Shenker, Dotsenko, Fateev and others is outside the supplied names.
